Prior to going into closed session, the City Council will convene in the Auditorium serving as Council Chambers to take public comment on the closed session items only. General public comment will be provided for during the regular portion of the meeting beginning at 7:30 P.M.

NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC FOR REGULAR MEETING
Copies of staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business referred to on the Agenda are on file in the Office of the City Clerk and are available for public inspection at the City Library.
Persons who wish to speak during the Public Participation portion of the Agenda, shall fill out a card requesting to speak and shall submit it to the City Clerk prior to the start of the City Council meeting. When called, each person may address any item on or off the agenda during the public participation.
In compliance with Government Code Section 54957.5, copies of staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business referred to on the Agenda are on file in the Office of the City Clerk - 213 E. Foothill Blvd.; copies for public view are at the Azusa City Library - 729 N. Dalton Ave., Azusa Police Department Lobby - 725 N. Alameda Ave., and the City of Azusa Web Page www.azusaca.gov. Persons who wish to speak in-person during the Public Participation portion of the Agenda or on a Public Hearing item shall fill out a card requesting to speak and shall submit it to the City Clerk prior to 7:30 P.M.; cards submitted after this time will not be accepted.
Those wishing to participate during Public Comment may do so in-person at the Azusa Auditorium, or may submit written public comments by emailing PublicComment@azusaca.gov. Emailed public comments are due by 5:30 p.m. and shall be limited to no more than 250 words. Written public comments will be provided to the City Council and will be part of the record but will not be read aloud.
View the City Council meeting live on the City’s website https://www.azusaca.gov/1389/Watch-Meetings-Online, or on Channel 3 (Spectrum). Archived video of recorded meetings is also available on the City website.
Notice Regarding California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determinations. Pursuant to CEQA, a "project" is defined as a "whole action" subject to a public agency's discretionary funding or approval that has the potential to either (1) cause a direct physical change in the environment or (2) cause a reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change in the environment. "Projects" include discretionary activity by a public agency, a private activity that receives any public funding, or activities that involve the public agency's issuance of a discretionary approval and is not statutorily or categorically exempt from CEQA. (Pub. Res. Code § 21065.)   To the extent that matters listed in this Agenda are considered “projects” under CEQA, their appropriate CEQA determination will be listed below each recommendation.  If no CEQA determination is listed, it has been determined that the action does not constitute a “project” under CEQA.

This time has been set aside for persons in the audience to make public comments on items listed or not listed on this Agenda. Members of the audience will have the opportunity to address the City Council/Agency Board about public hearing items at the time the public hearing is held. Under the provisions of the Brown Act, the Council/Agency Board is prohibited from taking action on oral requests, but may refer the matter to staff or to a subsequent meeting. Each person or representative of a group shall be allowed to speak without interruption for up to five (5) continuous minutes, subject to compliance with applicable meeting rules. Questions to the speaker or responses to the speaker's questions or comments may be handled after the speaker has completed his/her comments. Public Participation will be limited to sixty (60) minutes.

1. CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATORS - Pursuant to California Government

City Council Minutes  Page | 1
March 2, 2026
 Staff Members: City Manager Gonzalez, City Attorney Richman, Deputy City Manager DeAnda-Scaia, Chief
of Police Wenrick, Director of Administrative Services Johnson, Director of Economic & Community
Development Jimenez, Director of I.T. Guadagnino, Planning Manager Vizcarra, Community Improvement
Manager Edson, City Librarian Hassen.

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Alayna Funes and Cataleya Cuevas.

The Invocation was led by Pastor Daniel Simonson, Christbridge Immanuel Church.

CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Richman reported that no reportable action was taken in Closed Session.

CEREMONIAL

Proclamation Declaring March as Women’s History Month

Councilmember Bow presented the proclamation and invited all women in attendance to join her for a photo in
honor of Women’s History Month.

Recognition of Azusa Youth Boxing Club

Mayor Alvarez presented a certificate in recognition of Efrain “Nuno” Romero to family members, and
Councilmember Gonzales presented a letter of sympathy to the Romero family.

Recognition of Azusa Raiders Cheer - Gremlin Division

Mayor Alvarez presented certificates of recognition to the Azusa Raiders Gremlin Division cheerleaders, and
their coaches in recognition of their multiple achievements.

Neha Upadhyaya, from the office of Senator Susan Rubio, presented the cheerleaders with a certificate of
recognition.

PUBLIC PARTICIPATION

Azusa Unified School District Superintendent, Arturo Otega shared highlights of Azusa High School fall sports;
congratulated the Gladstone Middle School students who placed in the track meet and the annual Lone Hill
Math Competition; announced that the Azusa Unified School District Classified Employee of the Year was
celebrated in January; and thanked all district employees for their hard work; mentioned that the Board of
Education retained a search firm, Leadership Associates, to assist in the search for a new superintendent.

Jack Ochoa, Los Angeles County Small Business Advocate, addressed the Council to express the need for more
certified businesses in the City; and noted that he is working with the Chamber to help bring more business to
the area.

Members of the Azusa Chamber of Commerce announced the successful completion of their first Launch
Business Academy cohort, with 22 businesses completing the seven-week program; mentioned they also
assisted 22 additional businesses in becoming certified; noted that Azusa has expressed interest in participating
in the FIFA World Cup 2026, ensuring local small businesses are prepared to engage in global opportunities;
and provided an update on the continued growth of regional partnerships.

Art Vasquez, a small business owner, expressed his gratitude toward the Azusa Chamber of Commerce for its
Launch Academy; stated that the program provided the appropriate tools needed for success and commended
the organization for its hard work.

REPORTS, UPDATES, AND ANNOUNCEMENTS FROM STAFF/COUNCIL

City Manager Communications - None.

Councilmember Announcements
City Council Minutes  Page | 2
March 2, 2026
 Mayor Pro Tem Avila announced that the Azusa academic scholarship program opened on March 2;
highlighted upcoming free seminars including “Healthy Living for Brain and Body” on March 4, “Healthy
Relationships” on March 5, and “Stress Relief: Emotional Well-Being” on March 11; reported on the “Lucky in
March” socials held on March 12 at the North Recreation Center and Gladstone Park; shared that he attended
the 2026 Independent Cities Winter Seminar from February 20 to February 22; and congratulated staff on
organizing a successful Lunar New Year event.

Councilmember Mendez announced upcoming library events; inquired about the proposed 50-cent tax measure
and whether it would be brought forward for Council discussion; also questioned about the potential
establishment of a downtown business district, noting it may be an appropriate time to explore the idea.

Staff responded that a letter of opposition had been submitted regarding the Tax Measure, but if the Council
concurred, he could provide an update and facilitate a discussion; and agreed about the downtown business
district and suggested placing the item on a future strategic planning session agenda.

Councilmember Mendez reported attending the Independent Cities Winter Seminar from February 20 to 22.

Councilmember Bow shared several announcements, including a “Health and Nutrition” class for seniors at Cal
Poly Pomona in conjunction with Azusa Community Resources, held every second and fourth Wednesday of
the month; highlighted additional upcoming health and wellness activities, including the One Legacy 5K
Run/Walk on April 25; reported attending the Independent Cities Winter Seminar on February 20-22; stated she
attended the San Gabriel Valley State of Public Safety Luncheon; and congratulated City staff for their hard
work in organizing the Fourth Annual Lunar New Year celebration.

Councilmember Gonzales announced the opening of registration for the Youth Soccer Program; mentioned a
family field trip scheduled for March 28 to the Palm Springs Aerial Tramway; and reported attending the
Independent Cities Winter Seminar held February 20–22; requested that certificates be prepared for the Azusa
High School Girls’ Soccer Team in recognition of being CIF finalists and asked that the item be placed on a
future agenda; also requested clarification regarding the Azusa Chamber of Commerce and certified businesses
within the City; and congratulated the Council of Governments (COG) on increased security measures at Metro
stations, including the installation of fare turnstiles to reduce fare evasion.

Mayor Alvarez announced recent activities at the Azusa City Library, including Family Craft Hour events held
on March 10 and March 17; reported his attendance at the Independent Cities Winter Seminar on February 20–
22; mentioned the grand opening of Panera Bread on February 20; highlighted the well-attended Lunar New
Year Celebration; also reported attending a Foothill Transit Workshop, and announced the new Foothill Transit
Center at Cal Poly Pomona; and addressed the proposed Los Angeles County sales tax measure, noting that a
letter of opposition had been submitted.

SCHEDULED ITEMS

RECEIVE AN UPDATE AND PROVIDE DIRECTION REGARDING THE  POSSIBLE
REDEVELOPMENT OF THE ATLANTIS GARDENS HOUSING DEVELOPMENT

Director of Economic and Community Development Jimenez provided a brief update on the Atlantis Garden
property, including a history of redevelopment discussions dating back to 2010.

Founder and Principal of City Fabrick, Brian Ulechefski, and Chief Development Officer of National CORE,
Alexa Washburn, expressed their enthusiasm to partner with the City to implement a vision for transforming
Atlantis Garden into a mixed-income community featuring homeownership opportunities and affordable senior
housing; presented an early conceptual vision of the redevelopment and were available to answer Council
questions.

The Council raised questions regarding property ownership within the area, concerns about existing housing
conditions, and the impact of developing new housing adjacent to older, less-maintained properties.
Councilmembers inquired about the developers’ experience with similar projects and requested clarification
regarding the proposed parking structure and asked for elaboration on residential density. Additionally,
recommendations were made to consider incorporating multiple entrances to the development and designing
housing that appears less apartment-style in character.

City Council Minutes  Page | 3
March 2, 2026
 Mr. Ulechefski responded that new development often encourages surrounding property owners to reinvest and
improve their properties, noting that this approach has been successfully implemented in other National CORE
projects; stated that the majority of the housing units would be allotted two parking spaces, while senior housing
would be provided with one space per unit; explained that existing properties in the area have an approximate
density of 28 units per acre, while the proposed senior development would have a density of approximately 8
units per acre and the townhomes approximately 24 units per acre, with surrounding properties having
comparable densities.

Moved by Councilmember Gonzales and seconded by Councilmember Bow and carried by unanimous vote of
the Council to: Receive and file a status update regarding ongoing negotiations with National CORE under the
Exclusive Negotiating Agreement; and Review and provide direction on the preliminary conceptual
development plans for Atlantis Gardens; and Determine that the adoption of this request does not qualify as a
“project” as defined in California Environmental Quality Act (Public Resources Code Section 21000 et seq.)
(“CEQA”) Section 15378.
